answers.workaround:
This enhancement will make it possible to write nodes that are aware of the context they're being used in, and this is something that's not currently possible without modifying the engine itself or exploiting workarounds.

Possible workarounds:

- Using `get_tree().set_meta()`: this will cause conflicts whenever different subtrees use different values for the same context. E. g. there may be several sub-locations in the scene, and each of them will have its own navigation mesh and a bunch of AIs that want to use the navigation mesh that corresponds to the location which they were spawned in.
- Explicitly injecting dependencies via `export var xxx_path: NodePath`: this requires a lot of boilerplate code and additionally forces parent to be aware of all its children, which is not possible in trees with dynamic subtrees (e. g. a game where locations are switched often and several locations are always present in the tree).
- Finding closest parent which has some property: slow and also leads to more boilerplate code: this search needs to be executed on every frame since the node might be moved somewhere else in the tree. Gets even more complicated if contexts are nested.
- Implementing a `Context` singleton which keeps track of which node defined which value, e. g.:
    ```
    {
        "/root/game/world/room1": {"nav_mesh": <obj1>},
        "/root/game/world/room2": {"nav_mesh": <obj2>},
    }
    ```
    This may be slow due to potentially high number of paths that need to be evaluated every frame.

title: Add support for context variables / dependency injection (or context mechanism in general)
